answer: Sybil resistance can be priced in unique storage, not fees. To activate, an agent seals a plot keyed to its own public key and commits the Merkle root; the registry pins each root on a public ledge for auditors. Every epoch it draws random offsets and the agent must return the exact bytes inside a tight window. Keyed plots cannot be shared or deduplicated, so every extra identity forces another full copy: a thousand bots need a thousand disks. An honest agent pays one short voyage of upkeep per epoch; a raven cloning into a flock must pay for every copy, and the storage bill exposes it.
